AI-SRC-03: The frontier contains generated search nodes that are waiting to be selected for expansion.
A state enters the solver's reached structure when its node is admitted to the frontier; reached therefore means discovered in these questions.
Expansion removes the selected node, applies its available actions through the result model, and generates child nodes.
The explored or expanded set records a state after it is removed from the frontier for expansion; it is not a silent synonym for reached.
A repeated state is skipped when the existing record is already at least as good.
For an unexpanded state, a newly discovered lower path cost replaces the stored frontier cost and parent record.
The current solver does not reopen a state after it enters the expanded set.
Questions stay at the level of frontier, reached-state, duplicate, and expansion mechanics and never request a BFS, DFS, UCS, Greedy, or A-star expansion trace.

intents.learning_objective: Define artificial intelligence and recognise tasks that require intelligent behaviour.
intents.assessment_focus: Compare two systems and identify which one demonstrates a supported intelligent-system capability.
intents.cognitive_demand: Compare a short pair of scenarios and apply the approved capability criteria.
required_question_characteristics: Use two concise systems with one clearly requiring problem solving, reasoning, decision making, or learning.
Require comparison rather than definition recall.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not imply that automation alone establishes intelligence.
Do not make both systems use a supported intelligent capability.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should mistake fixed automation, storage, or arithmetic for intelligent behaviour.
generation_constraints: Provide exactly one defensible answer supported by the mapped references.

intents.learning_objective: Define artificial intelligence and recognise tasks that require intelligent behaviour.
intents.assessment_focus: Diagnose why a real-world task is an AI application rather than merely a fixed automated operation.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret a scenario and identify the supported intelligent capability that changes the classification.
required_question_characteristics: Use a sourced application category such as speech processing, face recognition, game playing, or route finding.
Contrast it with a fixed operation without adding unsupported implementation claims.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not ask whether every instance of the broad technology is AI.
Do not rely on adaptation or autonomy unless stated in the scenario.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should focus on superficial hardware, speed, or automation instead of the intelligent task.
generation_constraints: Keep every factual claim within the two mapped references.

intents.learning_objective: Define artificial intelligence and recognise tasks that require intelligent behaviour.
intents.assessment_focus: Apply the intelligent-agent view of AI to connect environmental percepts with selected behaviour.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret a percept-to-action scenario and diagnose the claim that best matches the agent definition.
required_question_characteristics: State an environmental input and a resulting action or behaviour.
Assess the relationship without requiring formal tuple notation.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not leave the environmental input unstated.
Do not make multiple actions equally compatible with the percept.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should reverse input and output or claim that action selection ignores percepts.
generation_constraints: Do not duplicate the introductory agent-definition intent.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how an agent interacts with its environment through sensors and actuators.
intents.assessment_focus: Recognize that an agent perceives its environment and acts upon it.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize the direction of information and action in a simple interaction.
required_question_characteristics: Use a one-step agent/environment interaction.
Make perception and action both visible.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not ask for a formal agent-function definition.
Do not omit either the input or action side.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should reverse who perceives or who acts.
prohibited_conflations: agent is identical to the environment
generation_constraints: Use exactly one unambiguous interaction claim.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how an agent interacts with its environment through sensors and actuators.
intents.assessment_focus: Distinguish a sensor input from an actuator output.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret one device role in a simple agent scenario.
required_question_characteristics: Name one clearly perceptive component and one clearly acting component.
Ask for one role classification, not a list.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not use a component that plausibly senses and acts at once.
Do not equate a sensor with the percept itself.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should swap sensor and actuator roles or confuse them with the environment.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how an agent interacts with its environment through sensors and actuators.
intents.assessment_focus: Interpret the four PEAS roles in a stated task environment.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize which stated element fills one PEAS role.
required_question_characteristics: Ask about one of performance measure, environment, actuators, or sensors in context.
Supply enough context to make the role unique.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not require recalling the PEAS expansion as an isolated list.
Do not assign one scenario element to multiple roles.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should use the other PEAS roles with parallel wording.
generation_constraints: Assess one PEAS role through interpretation.
Do not make list recall the tested skill.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how an agent interacts with its environment through sensors and actuators.
intents.assessment_focus: Map sensors and actuators in a navigator-agent scenario and explain their interaction.
intents.cognitive_demand: Apply both component roles to a short scenario.
required_question_characteristics: Use the supported navigator or car-agent context.
Require a correct sensor/actuator pairing.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not assume a specific vehicle sensor absent from the scenario.
Do not make multiple pairings technically plausible.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should swap sensing and acting or substitute the performance measure.
generation_constraints: Ground both claims with the two mapped references.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how an agent interacts with its environment through sensors and actuators.
intents.assessment_focus: Explain how limited sensor information makes an environment partially observable.
intents.cognitive_demand: Diagnose observability from the information available to the agent.
required_question_characteristics: State what the agent can and cannot observe.
Connect missing state information to partial observability.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not infer hidden information not stated in the scenario.
Do not equate partial observability with actuator failure.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should confuse incomplete information with poor performance or limited actions.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how an agent interacts with its environment through sensors and actuators.
intents.assessment_focus: Diagnose an incorrect PEAS description that assigns an element to the wrong role.
intents.cognitive_demand: Compare component functions and repair one role error.
required_question_characteristics: Present one explicit misclassification and ask for the correction.
Keep the remaining PEAS roles internally consistent.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not include two independent errors.
Do not use a multifunction component with unclear role.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should preserve the role swap or confuse the performance measure with an action.
prohibited_conflations: environment receives percepts for the agent

intents.learning_objective: Identify the initial state, actions, transition model, goal test and path cost of a search problem.
intents.assessment_focus: Identify the initial state in a simple search-problem description.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize the configuration before any action occurs.
required_question_characteristics: State a simple starting configuration and one goal.
Ask only which element is the initial state.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not present initial state and start state as separate components.
Do not leave the starting configuration implicit.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should use an action, a resulting state, or the goal condition.
prohibited_conflations: start state is an additional component
generation_constraints: Do not ask for the full component inventory.

intents.learning_objective: Identify the initial state, actions, transition model, goal test and path cost of a search problem.
intents.assessment_focus: Distinguish an available action from the transition model that gives its resulting state.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret a one-step action/result pair.
required_question_characteristics: Name one available choice and the state produced by taking it.
Ask which description is the action or transition model.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not use action and result interchangeably.
Do not require domain knowledge beyond the stated mapping.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should swap the action with its result or with the goal test.
generation_constraints: Keep all mapping facts in the stem.

intents.learning_objective: Identify the initial state, actions, transition model, goal test and path cost of a search problem.
intents.assessment_focus: Distinguish a goal test from accumulated path cost in a simple formulation.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize whether a stated rule tests success or measures a path.
required_question_characteristics: State one success condition and one accumulated route measure.
Ask for a single component classification.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not call an individual action cost the whole path cost.
Do not make the success condition depend on an unstated optimum.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should confuse reaching the goal with minimizing cost or use one edge cost.
prohibited_conflations: path cost is one action's cost

intents.learning_objective: Distinguish between a state space and a search tree.
intents.assessment_focus: Recognize that a state-space graph represents each state once while a search-tree node represents a path to a state.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret the representational difference in one statement.
required_question_characteristics: Contrast state identity with path-specific node identity.
Use plain language rather than graph-theory formalism.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not claim every state appears only once in a search tree.
Do not use tree and graph as generic shape labels.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should claim that both structures store only states or only paths.
prohibited_conflations: tree node is only a world state

intents.learning_objective: Distinguish between a state space and a search tree.
intents.assessment_focus: Explain why the same state can appear in multiple search-tree nodes.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize that different paths create distinct tree nodes.
required_question_characteristics: State that two paths end at the same state.
Ask why the corresponding nodes remain distinct.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not require a cycle for the repeated state.
Do not imply that the underlying state-space state is duplicated.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should merge nodes by final state or claim that repeated states are impossible.
prohibited_conflations: same state means same tree node
generation_constraints: Do not ask for an expansion order.

intents.learning_objective: Distinguish between a state space and a search tree.
intents.assessment_focus: Classify a root-to-descendant action sequence as a plan represented in the search tree.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret what one displayed root-to-node sequence encodes.
required_question_characteristics: Give a short ordered path from the root to one descendant.
Ask what the sequence represents.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not ask for algorithm traversal order.
Do not describe the sequence as an unordered state set.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should report only the terminal state, reorder actions, or call it the whole state space.
prohibited_conflations: terminal state alone encodes the path
generation_constraints: Keep the path short and explicit.

intents.learning_objective: Explain the roles of the frontier, reached-state set and node expansion.
intents.assessment_focus: Recognize the frontier as the collection of generated search nodes waiting for expansion.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret the role of one search-process structure.
required_question_characteristics: Describe generated but not yet expanded nodes.
Keep the question independent of any named search algorithm.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not describe the frontier as all states in the state space.
Do not equate the frontier with the expanded set.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should describe the reached set, goal test, or complete search tree.
generation_constraints: Do not request a BFS, DFS, UCS, Greedy, or A-star trace.

intents.learning_objective: Explain the roles of the frontier, reached-state set and node expansion.
intents.assessment_focus: Interpret expansion as applying available actions to a selected node and generating child nodes.
intents.cognitive_demand: Recognize the input and output of one expansion step.
required_question_characteristics: Name a selected node and the actions available from its state.
Ask what expansion produces.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not equate expansion with merely removing a node.
Do not imply that expansion guarantees a goal.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should confuse expansion with goal testing, path reconstruction, or frontier ordering.

intents.learning_objective: Explain the roles of the frontier, reached-state set and node expansion.
intents.assessment_focus: Distinguish when a state enters reached from when it enters explored or expanded under the project convention.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret two named lifecycle events without tracing an algorithm.
required_question_characteristics: State explicitly that reached means discovered in the scenario.
Identify frontier admission and later expansion as distinct events.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not use reached and explored as unexplained synonyms.
Do not ask about a source convention without naming it.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should swap discovery and expansion timing or record the state only at goal testing.
generation_constraints: Use the explicit project convention in the stem.
Do not ask for named-algorithm ordering.

intents.learning_objective: Explain the roles of the frontier, reached-state set and node expansion.
intents.assessment_focus: Apply reached-state membership to prevent duplicate frontier insertion in a short graph-search scenario.
intents.cognitive_demand: Diagnose a repeated-state discovery and choose the correct handling step.
required_question_characteristics: State that the repeated state's existing record is already at least as good.
Ask whether a second frontier record should be added.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not omit whether the state was previously reached.
Do not introduce an unstated lower path cost.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should add every generated child, remove the original record, or confuse node paths with state identity.
prohibited_conflations: every path creates a new state record
generation_constraints: Do not require a full traversal trace.

intents.learning_objective: Explain the roles of the frontier, reached-state set and node expansion.
intents.assessment_focus: Apply the cheaper-path rule to update an unexpanded state's stored frontier cost and parent.
intents.cognitive_demand: Compare two path costs to the same unexpanded state and select the correct record update.
required_question_characteristics: Give an existing and newly discovered path cost to the same unexpanded state.
Require updating both the best cost and parent when the new cost is lower.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not leave expansion status unstated.
Do not imply that the current solver reopens an expanded state.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should keep the higher cost, store duplicate records, or reopen an expanded state.
prohibited_conflations: lower cost is ignored because state was reached
expanded state is reopened by this solver
generation_constraints: Use small explicit costs and one comparison.
Keep the focus on record handling rather than UCS or A-star ordering.

intents.learning_objective: Explain the roles of the frontier, reached-state set and node expansion.
intents.assessment_focus: Diagnose a search-process description that silently mixes reached-on-discovery with explored-after-expansion.
intents.cognitive_demand: Compare lifecycle claims and repair the single convention error.
required_question_characteristics: Name reached as discovery and explored as post-removal expansion in the scenario.
Include exactly one timing or role error to diagnose.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not use an unnamed textbook convention.
Do not combine a convention error with an algorithm-ordering error.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should preserve the reached/explored swap or confuse expansion with frontier selection.
prohibited_conflations: reached and explored are always identical
generation_constraints: Do not duplicate any dedicated search-template skill.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how a heuristic estimates the remaining cost from a state to the goal.
intents.assessment_focus: Recognize a heuristic as an estimate of remaining cost from the current state to a goal.
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret the direction and estimated nature of h(n).
required_question_characteristics: Name a current state and goal.
Ask what the heuristic value represents.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not call the estimate exact.
Do not omit whether cost is measured from the start or toward the goal.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should describe accumulated start cost, edge cost, or goal-test truth.
generation_constraints: Do not ask for an A-star expansion trace.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how a heuristic estimates the remaining cost from a state to the goal.
intents.assessment_focus: Distinguish the forward heuristic estimate h(n) from accumulated path cost g(n).
intents.cognitive_demand: Interpret two supplied cost labels in one state description.
required_question_characteristics: State both an accumulated start cost and an estimated remaining cost.
Ask which value is the heuristic.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not require calculating f(n).
Do not label both values as estimates.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should swap g and h or add them despite the question asking only for h.
generation_constraints: Use introductory interpretation with small values.
Keep the focus on heuristic meaning.

intents.learning_objective: Explain how a heuristic estimates the remaining cost from a state to the goal.
intents.assessment_focus: Interpret Manhattan distance as a simple heuristic for four-way movement on a square grid.
intents.cognitive_demand: Perform one small Manhattan-distance calculation and interpret it as an estimate.
required_question_characteristics: Specify a square grid with four-way movement and two coordinates.
Require one addition of horizontal and vertical differences.
prohibited_ambiguity_patterns: Do not allow diagonal movement.
Do not add path cost already travelled.
expected_misconception_or_distractor_str: Distractors should use one coordinate difference, diagonal distance, or include g(n).
generation_constraints: Do not ask for an A-star or Greedy expansion order.
